stem: Why should you periodically review your service charges?
options: To see if they compare with market competition
Because regulators require a new fee every year
To make sure every account pays the same fee
So you can raise them at every review
why: The deposits slide calls for periodic review of DDA service charges compared to market competition.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 5

flashcard.front: Why should you periodically review your service charges?
flashcard.back: To see if they compare with market competition

keyFact: Review service charges: to compare with market competition

stem: Which of these should you consider when monitoring your CD program?
options: Current market rates for your locations
why: For CDs, monitor exception rate increases above current stated rates, early withdrawal penalty waivers, and current market rates for your locations.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 5

flashcard.front: What are some things to consider when monitoring your CD program?
flashcard.back: Exception rates, early withdrawal penalty waivers, current market rates for your locations

keyFact: CD program, watch: exception rates, early withdrawal penalty waivers, current market rates for your locations

stem: Why do you review your deposit program?
options: To see how it compares with market competition, whether it's priced within or outside of market scope, and its fees
To decide which branches to close based on how many deposit accounts each one holds
To set loan approval limits for each lender based on the deposits they bring in
To count how many accounts each employee opened for incentive pay
why: For DDAs, compare service charges with market competition and check whether products are priced within or outside of market scope.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 5

flashcard.front: Why do you review your deposit program?
flashcard.back: To see if they compare with market competition, priced within or outside of market scope, fees

keyFact: Review deposit program: compare with competition, priced within or outside market scope, fees

stem: Which is listed as the largest non-interest expense?
why: Personnel is the largest expense. The deck says to review job grades, salaries, and benefits, and keep overtime at a minimum.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 6

stem: Managing personnel expense includes keeping overtime at a minimum.
why: Managing staff means staying within the number of hours required for the employee or position and keeping overtime at a minimum.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 6

stem: Which of these is NOT listed as a popular treasury management service?
why: Collateral inspection fees are listed under loan income. ACH origination, RDC, and Positive Pay are treasury management services.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 2

stem: Which of these is listed as a source of loan income?
why: Loan income includes coupon books, Skip-A-Payment programs, doc fees, unused or renewal fees on LOCs, collateral inspection fees, and late fees. The others are treasury management services.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 3

stem: As of July 1, 2026, what maximum late fee does the deck show?
why: The slide notes that the state updates the minimum and maximum late fees annually.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 3

keyFact: Late fee max (as of 2026-07-01): 5% of the unpaid installment or $34.00

stem: The minimum and maximum a bank can charge for late fees is updated every five years.
why: The slide says the minimum and maximum are updated annually.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 3

stem: Which of these is listed under vendor contract management?
why: Vendor contract management covers auto-renewal pricing, contract expiration and renewal dates, review, and negotiation.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 4

stem: For DDAs, the deck suggests pushing e-statements and charging for paper statements.
why: The deposits slide asks whether you are pushing e-statements and charging for paper statements, and suggests reward accounts to entice new generational customers.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 5

stem: Consumer and business debit cards are described as an "old" product but a good income generator.
why: Interchange fees and reviewing card service provider reports to maximize card usage are listed with it.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 5

stem: Which of these is NOT listed under accountability for fee waivers?
why: Fee waiver accountability covers the NSF/OD refund report, check order waivers and refunds, miscellaneous item fees, waived service charges, and early withdrawal penalties. Interchange is debit card income.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 6

options: Number of branch visits per month
Number of fee waivers per account
Number of online logins per customer
why: The deck asks whether we are fully using our products and services based on their cost.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 7

keyFact: Customer stickiness: track number of products per household

stem: Which of these is part of the structured system for expenses that worked for the presenter's bank?
why: The structured system for expenses includes annual department budgets, bank officer expenses, and centralized supply ordering.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 7

stem: What efficiency ratio did the presenter's bank report as of 9/30/26?
why: Increased efficiency (working smarter, not harder) is listed first under what has worked for the bank.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 7

stem: Why does the presenter say it is not easy for a community bank to increase fee income?
why: Everyone offers pretty much the same thing. Expenses, by contrast, can be managed through consistent review and effort.

source.ref: Bank Income and Expense deck, handout page 8
